say: Before you blame life, check the three things you control.
All day, a chemical called adenosine builds up in your brain and makes you sleepy.
Cut sleep short, and you start the day with yesterday's leftovers.
It hides it, and then it eats into your sleep.
About half of it is still in you at eleven.
Bright light at night, even room light, tells your body clock it's still day,
so your sleep signal comes later.
For a seven a.m. alarm: in bed by eleven, last coffee by two, lights low from eight.
Low iron or your thyroid can cause it, and coffee fixes neither.
